title: Ajay Devgn's Two ₹50-Crore Shots: Drishyam 3 and Golmaal 5 Eye Historic Openings
excerpt: Ajay Devgn has two 2026 releases left — Drishyam 3 on October 2 and Golmaal 5 — and both carry expectations of a historic ₹50-crore opening day, a feat only Shah Rukh Khan and Hrithik Roshan have managed twice.
body:
• Ajay Devgn has two major releases left in 2026 — Drishyam 3 on October 2 and Golmaal 5 — and both carry historic opening-day expectations.
  • The milestone in play is scoring two ₹50-crore opening days, a club that currently holds only Shah Rukh Khan (Pathaan, Jawan) and Hrithik Roshan (War, War 2).
  • Drishyam 3 could deliver Devgn's career-best opening, topping Singham Again's ₹43.7 crore, while Golmaal 5 has an outside shot at his first-ever ₹50-crore opener, according to Koimoi's box-office analysis.
  • Both films would need to cross ₹50 crore net on day one — a tall order, but the Gandhi Jayanti holiday and the Golmaal franchise's opening-day record give him a genuine shot.

A two-film shot at box-office history

Ajay Devgn is heading into the final quarter of 2026 with something few stars get in a single calendar year: two legitimate box-office events. Drishyam 3, the finale of his crime-thriller franchise, arrives in theaters on October 2, a Gandhi Jayanti national holiday. Golmaal 5, Rohit Shetty's fifth outing with his comedy ensemble, is expected later in the year. Together, they put Devgn within reach of a milestone only two Bollywood stars have managed: two ₹50-crore opening days.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=BSZZwBaNQAA

The math is simple and the bar is high. Shah Rukh Khan did it twice in 2023 — Pathaan at ₹57 crore and Jawan at ₹75 crore. Hrithik Roshan did it with War (₹53.35 crore) and War 2 (₹52.5 crore), per Koimoi's tracking. Devgn's personal best remains Singham Again's ₹43.7 crore. To join that club, both Drishyam 3 and Golmaal 5 would have to open above ₹50 crore net.

Where Devgn stands right now

Devgn has never had a ₹50-crore opener, but his opening-day graph keeps climbing: Golmaal Again took ₹30.14 crore in 2017, then the year's biggest Bollywood opening, and Singham Again pushed his record to ₹43.7 crore. Within the crime-thriller lane, Drishyam 2 opened at ₹15.38 crore and Raid 2 at ₹19.71 crore — the latter holding the post-COVID record for a Hindi crime thriller until Mirzapur: The Movie stormed in with ₹28.11 crore on September 4, 2026.

That sets up Drishyam 3's first target: anything above ₹28.2 crore reclaims the genre's opening-day crown, per Koimoi. Its second target is the Gandhi Jayanti chart, where War's ₹53.35 crore sits far above Bang Bang (₹27.54 crore) in second. Directed by Abhishek Pathak and produced by Panorama Studios, with Tabu, Shriya Saran and Rajat Kapoor returning alongside Devgn's Vijay Salgaonkar, the finale has the holiday advantage and what Koimoi describes as enormous brand value built over two films.

What each film needs to do

For Drishyam 3, the holiday is the X-factor. Koimoi's projections range from 35–40 crore to 45–50 crore after the trailer landed — either would be remarkable for a content-driven thriller. Fifty crore would be uncharted territory for the genre — but this is also the franchise whose second chapter grew its opening by sheer word of mouth, and Gandhi Jayanti has historically supercharged family audiences.

Golmaal 5 may actually be the more plausible ₹50-crore candidate. The franchise's day-one trend is one of Bollywood's steepest climbs: ₹2.32 crore for Golmaal, ₹5.89 crore for Golmaal Returns, ₹8.36 crore for Golmaal 3, and ₹30.14 crore for Golmaal Again. Stree 2's ₹64.8-crore opening proved a well-promoted comedy can do blockbuster numbers on day one. With the core ensemble returning and Sharman Joshi and Priyamani joining, Koimoi gives the film "an outside chance of hitting the 50 crore net milestone" if the trailer and promotions land.

"If the makers of Golmaal 5 managed to build a strong buzz with strong promotional assets, including a trailer, the film can do wonders on day 1 by crossing the 50 crore milestone."

— Koimoi, box-office analysis

The diaspora box-office factor

Opening-day records are no longer decided in India alone. Diaspora audiences in the United States, the UK and the Gulf contribute a meaningful share of Bollywood's biggest starts, and Devgn's core overseas base — the family audiences who turned Golmaal and Drishyam into durable brands abroad — will be central to any ₹50-crore bid.

What's next

Drishyam 3's trailer will be the first real signal of how high it can go — a strong promo could put Devgn's ₹43.7-crore record under immediate threat on October 2. Then all eyes shift to Golmaal 5's campaign and release date. If both films cross ₹50 crore on day one, Devgn joins Shah Rukh Khan and Hrithik Roshan in one of Bollywood's most exclusive clubs. If only one does, it is still likely to be the biggest opening of his career — and the story of 2026's box office either way.
